source_title: Schedule of Selected Releases 2026
concepts_supported: Official Eastern Time release timestamps; 08:30 CPI, PPI and Employment Situation; 10:00 JOLTS and other releases
main_result: Confirms that important BLS releases are scheduled at both 08:30 and 10:00 ET and that the calendar uses Eastern Time.
important_limitations: Current-year schedule only; revisions and shutdown-related changes require a point-in-time calendar archive.

source_title: Release Schedule
concepts_supported: Official release timestamps for GDP, personal income/outlays/PCE and trade
main_result: Shows major BEA releases, including GDP and Personal Income and Outlays, commonly scheduled for 08:30 ET.
important_limitations: Live schedule can change; historical event-study use requires archived dates and original release times.

source_title: U.S. Census Bureau Economic Indicator Release Schedule: List View
concepts_supported: 08:30 durable goods, retail sales and housing starts; 10:00 new-home sales, construction spending and inventories
main_result: Establishes that 10:00 ET contains genuine scheduled information arrivals as well as 08:30 releases.
important_limitations: Current calendar is not a surprise database and may contain rescheduled releases; archive snapshots are needed.

source_title: ISM PMI Reports
concepts_supported: 10:00 ET Manufacturing and Services PMI release timing; survey construction
main_result: Manufacturing PMI is released on the first business day at 10:00 ET; ISM describes industry-weighted survey panels.
important_limitations: Not a historical surprise series; ISM is a private association rather than a government agency.

source_title: US Consumer Confidence
concepts_supported: 10:00 ET Consumer Confidence release timing
main_result: The Conference Board states that the Consumer Confidence Index is published at 10:00 ET.
important_limitations: Historical forecast, actual and revision vintages are not supplied on this public landing page.

source_title: Meeting Calendars and Information
author_or_institution: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
concepts_supported: FOMC meeting dates and policy-statement documentation
main_result: FOMC decisions are separately timed information events and should not be mixed with the 08:30/09:30 study without controls.
important_limitations: FOMC statements are generally 14:00 ET, outside the requested morning window; unscheduled speeches still require a separate calendar.

source_title: Nasdaq Systems: Hours of Operation
concepts_supported: 09:30-16:00 ET Nasdaq market hours; extended system hours
main_result: Confirms that 09:30 ET is the formal U.S. cash-equity market open while Nasdaq systems operate before it.
important_limitations: Does not show that NQ futures reverse at 09:30 or that other assets inherit an edge.

source_title: Trading Information
concepts_supported: 09:30 ET core open auction; pre-opening order entry; 09:30-16:00 core session
main_result: Confirms that a concentrated opening auction occurs at 09:30 ET for cash equities.
important_limitations: Cash-equity auction mechanics do not apply directly to spot gold or continuously traded COMEX gold futures.

source_title: Gold Futures and Options Fact Card
concepts_supported: GC contract size, tick, physical settlement and near-round-the-clock Globex trading hours
main_result: GC trades from Sunday through Friday with only a daily maintenance break, so gold is already active before 09:30 ET.
important_limitations: Product documentation is not evidence of an intraday return anomaly or of spot-CFD execution quality.

source_title: COMEX Rulebook Chapter 113: Gold Futures
concepts_supported: GC deliverable contract and exchange time convention
main_result: Defines the 100-troy-ounce physically delivered GC contract and specifies New York time when otherwise unstated.
important_limitations: Rulebook terms do not establish price behavior at 08:30, 09:30 or 10:00.

source_title: Trading COMEX Gold and Silver
concepts_supported: London, New York and Shanghai gold centers; hourly GC volume context
main_result: Documents multiple global gold trading centers and supports treating gold as a global, not cash-equity-session-only, market.
important_limitations: Exchange-authored educational material; descriptive rather than causal research.

source_title: Impact of Macroeconomic News on Metal Futures
author_or_institution: John Elder, Hong Miao and Sanjay Ramchander
concepts_supported: Gold reaction to 08:30, 09:15 and 10:00 announcements; surprises; continuation versus sign response
market_studied: COMEX gold, silver and copper futures
main_result: The 08:30 announcement set had the largest impact on gold; NFP and durable-goods surprises were especially important. Some 10:00 releases also affected returns, and announcement effects dissipated within about 60 minutes.
important_limitations: Older regime; futures rather than retail XAUUSD; release-time mix changed; no 09:30-equity-open control and no ICT patterns.

source_title: Examining the Impact of Macroeconomic Announcements on Gold Futures in a VAR-GARCH Framework
author_or_institution: Lee A. Smales, Barry O'Grady and Yi Yang
concepts_supported: 08:30 macro-news effect; spreads, volatility, returns and volume; transaction costs
main_result: Major 08:30 announcements produced a sharp activity jump; the unconditional difference from non-announcement days became statistically indistinguishable within about three minutes. Higher volatility widened spreads and reduced volume.
important_limitations: Only selected major 08:30 announcements; historical pit/open timing; not spot XAUUSD and not a directional strategy test.

source_title: Do Macroeconomics News Releases Affect Gold and Silver Prices?
author_or_institution: Rohan Christie-David, Mukesh Chaudhry and Timothy W. Koch
concepts_supported: Announcement surprise effects; contradictory/modest evidence; rapid price adjustment
main_result: Gold responded to CPI, unemployment, GDP, PPI and capacity utilization, but metals reacted to fewer announcements than interest-rate futures; many releases had no detectable effect.
important_limitations: Old low-inflation sample, floor-trading hours and 15-minute aggregation obscure first-minute dynamics.

source_title: What Moves the Gold Market?
author_or_institution: Jun Cai, Yan-Leung Cheung and Michael C. S. Wong
concepts_supported: Intraday gold volatility seasonality and announcement effects
main_result: Intraday periodicity materially affects volatility; employment, GDP, CPI and personal-income announcements were the strongest of 23 releases.
important_limitations: Older floor-trading era; abstract-level public access here; does not test 09:30 manipulation or modern XAUUSD costs.

source_title: Who Sets the Price of Gold? London or New York
author_or_institution: Martin Hauptfleisch, Talis J. Putnins and Brian M. Lucey
concepts_supported: Gold futures-versus-spot price discovery; electronic trading; announcements
market_studied: COMEX futures and London OTC spot gold
data_frequency: One-second data aggregated to hourly price-discovery estimates
main_result: COMEX contributed more to gold price discovery on average; after near-24-hour Globex adoption, floor-opening/time-zone patterns weakened. US GDP increased futures information leadership, while employment news increased quote noise.
important_limitations: Hourly event indicators cannot isolate 08:30 versus 09:30; institutional London spot data are not a retail XAUUSD feed.

source_title: How Do Macroeconomic News Surprises Affect Round-the-Clock Price Discovery of Gold?
author_or_institution: Neharika Sobti, Sanjay Sehgal and Balakrishnan Ilango
concepts_supported: Round-the-clock gold price discovery; news-surprise size, asymmetry and state dependence
market_studied: COMEX, London OTC and Shanghai gold futures
main_result: US futures led global price discovery; the New York-London overlap was most informative; large and dispersed US surprises had asymmetric, state-dependent effects.
important_limitations: Paywalled full text; session-level results do not establish a standalone 09:30 effect or an ICT setup.

source_title: The Timing of the Flight to Gold: An Intra-Day Analysis of Gold and the S&P 500
author_or_institution: Dirk G. Baur and Konstantin Kuck
concepts_supported: Gold response to extreme equity shocks; cross-asset risk sentiment
market_studied: Spot gold, gold futures and S&P 500
main_result: Extreme negative five-minute S&P 500 returns led positive gold responses, supporting a fast flight-to-gold channel.
important_limitations: Conditions on extreme equity losses, not all 09:30 opens; correlation/lead response does not imply predictable routine reversals.

source_title: Stop-Loss Orders and Price Cascades in Currency Markets
author_or_institution: Carol L. Osler / Federal Reserve Bank of New York
source_type: Reputable working paper with transparent methodology
concepts_supported: Stop clustering, liquidity levels, continuation versus reversal, opposing evidence to automatic sweep reversal
data_frequency: Minute quotes plus documented dealer orders; bootstrap tests
main_result: Exchange rates trended unusually rapidly after reaching stop-loss clusters; stop-loss responses were larger and longer than take-profit responses. This supports cascades/continuation, not an automatic reversal narrative.
important_limitations: FX, not gold; round-number order data from one historical dealer sample; does not validate ICT intent claims.

source_title: A Comparison of Trading and Non-Trading Mechanisms for Price Discovery
author_or_institution: Michael J. Barclay and Terrence Hendershott
concepts_supported: Nasdaq pre-open and 09:30 price discovery; efficient-opening counterpoint
main_result: As pre-open volume grew, opening prices became more efficient and price discovery shifted into the pre-open for the highest-volume stocks.
important_limitations: Cash stocks in an older market structure; does not cover NQ futures or gold and does not test reversal profitability.

source_title: The Short-Run Dynamics of the Price Adjustment to New Information
author_or_institution: Louis H. Ederington and Jae Ha Lee
concepts_supported: Efficient rapid adjustment after macro releases; counterpoint to predictable post-news reversal
main_result: Price adjustment began within 10 seconds and was essentially complete within about 40 seconds for the studied announcements.
important_limitations: Not gold; historical futures microstructure; rapid average adjustment does not rule out conditional intraday continuation/reversal.

source_title: What Drives Gold Prices?
concepts_supported: Gold relationships with real rates, inflation expectations and pessimism/risk sentiment
market_studied: LBMA gold and U.S. macro/financial variables
data_frequency: Annual, quarterly and limited daily regressions
main_result: Gold was negatively associated with expected long-term real rates and positively associated with pessimistic expectations; the authors stress correlation rather than causality.
important_limitations: Primarily low-frequency; cannot determine five-minute post-release pathways or execution rules.

source_title: Evaluating Qaurum: Why Simple Isn't Always Best
concepts_supported: Gold, real yields and U.S. dollar; multi-driver framing
main_result: Argues that real yields and the dollar are important but insufficient alone; demand, positioning and other drivers matter.
important_limitations: Industry body; proprietary inputs and low frequency; not causal evidence for a morning entry rule.

source_title: ICT NQ Futures Strategy: Bias, Kill Zones, and CISD Entry
concepts_supported: Nasdaq pre-market sweep; 09:30 displacement; HTF bias and confirmation
main_result: Defines a practitioner sequence of pre-market sweep, 09:30 displacement and later confirmation.
important_limitations: No transparent backtest, sample, costs or falsification; marketing language and institutional-intent claims are unverified.

source_title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Notes
author_or_institution: Community summary of Inner Circle Trader material
concepts_supported: 09:30 first move opposite eventual trend; liquidity, FVG and New York session narrative
main_result: Records the practitioner claim that the first move after 09:30 often opposes the eventual session trend.
important_limitations: Derivative notes rather than the primary lecture; qualitative wording; no denominator, controls or costs.

source_title: Fair Value Gap (FVG): ICT Strategy and Backtest Guide
concepts_supported: Three-candle FVG geometry; need for backtesting
main_result: Defines an FVG as non-overlap between candle-one and candle-three wicks around an impulsive middle candle and explicitly frames performance as a backtest question.
important_limitations: Commercial educator; claims about unfilled orders/institutional causes are not independently established.

source_title: Optimal Trade Entry
concepts_supported: OTE 62%-79% retracement zone and 70.5% reference
main_result: Defines OTE as the 62%-79% Fibonacci retracement of an impulse, often combined with an FVG or order block.
important_limitations: No empirical support for the privileged ratios; promotional and partly asserts institutional behavior.

source_title: ICT Rejection Block Explained
concepts_supported: Rejection-block wick zone
main_result: Defines a rejection block from a significant wick at a structural level, with the zone spanning the wick.
important_limitations: Significant wick, key level and institutional causation are subjective; no performance study.

source_title: ICT Judas Swing: How to Predict and Trade It
concepts_supported: Judas swing, AMD, 08:30-09:30 New York false-move hypothesis, 10:00 Silver Bullet
market_studied: FX, index futures and gold examples
main_result: Defines the New York Judas as a sharp 08:30-09:30 false move/sweep that may precede reversal and places a later entry window at 10:00-11:00.
important_limitations: No disclosed data or methodology; even examples list FOMC incorrectly among typical 08:30 releases; intent and frequency claims are unverified.

source_title: 10 AM Key Open Liquidity & Rejection Wick
concepts_supported: 10:00 key-open line; rejection wick; liquidity sweep; OTE and FVG confluence
main_result: Shows that '10 AM key open' is used in community tooling as the open of the 10:00 candle, not as an exchange-defined session open.
important_limitations: Closed-source script, no empirical validation, arbitrary defaults and no distinction from 10:00 economic releases.

source_title: ICT Silver Bullet Community Indicators
concepts_supported: 10:00-11:00 ET Silver Bullet time window and FVG
main_result: Community implementations consistently identify an AM Silver Bullet window of 10:00-11:00 ET.
important_limitations: Community aggregation, variable implementations and no proof of edge; a time window is not a formal market open.

source_title: Liquidity Sweep
concepts_supported: Sweep as breach followed by rapid return; distinction from genuine breakout
main_result: Provides a directly programmable practitioner description: breach an obvious high/low and return within one or two candles.
important_limitations: Stop locations and institutional intent are assumed, not observed; no outcome statistics.

source_title: ICT Market Structure Shift (MSS): How to Spot and Trade It
concepts_supported: Three-bar swings; displacement body close through a prior swing; FVG confluence
main_result: Defines MSS as a displacement-backed break of a prior swing and describes a three-candle swing convention.
important_limitations: Non-specialist trading source; no dataset, costs or proof; used only to capture terminology.

source_title: Structural Limits of OHLCV-Based Intraday Signals in MNQ Futures: A Systematic Falsification Study
concepts_supported: Critical test of opening, liquidity-grab, momentum and news OHLCV signals
main_result: None of fourteen signal families met all predeclared significance, cost, sample-size and multi-year stability criteria.
important_limitations: Very recent single-author preprint; methods and data require independent replication; fixed two-point cost; not gold.

source_title: How Do Gold Intra-Day Returns and Volatility React to Monetary Policy Shocks?
author_or_institution: Basel Awartani, Syed Mujahid Hussain and Nader Virk
concepts_supported: Gold response to FOMC shocks; asymmetry and multi-minute adjustment
main_result: Gold returns and volatility were more sensitive to looser than tighter FOMC shocks; adjustment continued beyond five minutes.
important_limitations: FOMC timing is outside the morning study; does not validate 08:30/09:30 ICT geometry.
